The factorization checks out: $(x^2+10x-36)^2 + (x+27)^2$ expands to $x^4+20x^3+29x^2-666x+2025$. The roots satisfy $x^2+10x-36 = \pm i(x+27)$, and the "+" branch gives $x^2+(10-i)x-(36+27i)=0$ with discriminant $243+88i$, so the roots are $\frac{-10+i\pm\sqrt{243+88i}}{2}$. With $\sqrt{243+88i}\approx 15.83+2.78i$, the root $\frac{-10+i+\sqrt{243+88i}}{2}\approx 2.92+1.89i$ lies in the first quadrant. The other roots are either in the fourth quadrant or have negative real part. The representation is unique because $66793$ is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{243+88i}$ is not in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ and no integer shift of the square root is possible. Thus $a=-10$, $b=1$, $c=243$, $d=88$, and $a+b+c+d=322$.
